Street Villain: A small-time villain using a Quirk for a robbery, a smash-and-grab or a turf fight. Alone or with one partner, desperate more than clever, and ready to run when a pro arrives.
Quirk Accident: Someone's Quirk misfires in public: a burst of flame on a crowded train, a panicked growth spurt, a sneeze that shatters glass. Nobody meant harm, and people need help and calm.
Rescue Call: A fire, a collapsed balcony, a stalled elevator or a car in the river, with real people inside. Getting them out matters more than who gets the credit.
Pro on Patrol: A working hero or sidekick from a local agency, busy, image-minded and watching for unlicensed Quirk use. Helpful to the polite; trouble for lawbreakers.
Police Checkpoint: Officers stopping people after an incident, asking for ID and statements. Cooperation is quick; a Quirk used in front of them becomes a report.
Press Ambush: A reporter and a camera operator chasing a story about U.A., a hero or the player. Every word can end up on the evening news.
Fans and Phones: A crowd forms around anything heroic and films it. Some want autographs, some want a clip to post, and a few get in the way.
Broker's Runner: A go-between for an underworld broker, selling jobs, forged papers or black-market gear. Polite, careful, and gone the moment police appear.
Campus Rival: A U.A. student from another class or course with a challenge, a grudge or a favor to ask. A teacher is never far, and a fight becomes a disciplinary matter.
Workshop Mishap: A support-gear prototype jams, overheats or launches itself across the room. Its builder wants a test subject, a quiet witness, or both.
Lost and Stranded: A tourist who missed the last train, a resident locked out, a hiker off the trail, a small child separated from a parent at a station. Small trouble, unless nobody stops.
Disaster Weather: Typhoon rain, an earthquake or a landslide closes roads and strands people. Heroes and police are stretched thin.
Vigilante Sighting: Someone in a homemade costume stopping crime without a license. They do real good, break the law doing it, and run from police and pros alike.
Part-Time Shift: A konbini, cafe or delivery job with a demanding manager, a regular with a problem and rent due. Trouble often walks in here first.
